title: Paragraph Numbering Scheme
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 2
notes: The strict six-level numbering scheme and its exceptions.

rules.title: Paragraphs use Arabic numerals followed by a full stop and tab
rules.description: A paragraph has an Arabic number, followed by a full stop and a tab space.

rules.title: Sub-paragraphs use lower case letters, block indented one tab
rules.description: A sub-paragraph is block indented one tab space and has a lower case letter followed by a full stop and tab space.

rules.title: Sub-sub-paragraphs use bracketed Arabic numerals
rules.description: A sub-sub-paragraph is block indented another tab space and has an Arabic number in brackets followed by a tab space.

rules.title: Sub-sub-sub-paragraphs use bracketed lower case Roman numerals
rules.description: A sub-sub-sub-paragraph is block indented another tab space and has a lower case Roman numeral in brackets followed by a tab space.

rules.title: Fifth-level paragraphs use lower case Roman numerals followed by tab
rules.description: A sub-sub-sub-sub-paragraph is block indented another tab space and has a lower case Roman number followed by a tab space.

rules.title: A single-paragraph document must not number the paragraph
rules.description: If a document has only one paragraph, that paragraph is not numbered and the first line of the next starts at the left margin.

rules.title: A paragraph must never have a single sub-paragraph
rules.description: A paragraph is never to have a single sub-paragraph.

rules.title: Condolence letter paragraphs are never numbered
rules.description: Paragraphs in letters of condolence should never be numbered.
rules.notes: Manual/contextual check: plugin cannot reliably detect a condolence letter; render as checklist item.

rules.title: Demi-Official letter paragraphs need not be numbered
rules.description: Paragraphs in DO letters need not be numbered.

rules.title: Letters to members of the public should not use paragraph numbers
rules.description: It would be unusual in letters to members of the public to number paragraphs.

rules.title: Annexes are lettered alphabetically in capitals
rules.description: Annexes are lettered alphabetically in capitals in the order in which they appear in the text; a single annex is lettered Annex A.

rules.title: Appendices are numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals
rules.description: Appendices are numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals in the order in which they appear; a single appendix is numbered Appendix 1.

rules.title: Annexes show the parent document reference at top right of first page
rules.description: Annexes show the identifying reference of the main document at the top right hand of the first page so they can be identified if detached.

check.where: Top right of the first page of each annex.

rules.notes: Evaluator must apply the pattern line-wise (MULTILINE) to the first page text, since the reference block occupies its own line.

rules.title: Annexes must be listed at the close of the parent document
rules.description: Annexes are listed at the close of the parent document under the heading 'Annexes:', the wording used being the same as their subject headings.

rules.title: Enclosures are listed numerically under 'Enclosure:'
rules.description: Enclosures are listed numerically at the end of the parent document under the heading 'Enclosure:' or 'Enclosures:'.

rules.title: Flags are listed alphabetically at the end of the parent document
rules.description: Flags are listed alphabetically at the end of the parent or covering document under the heading 'Flag:' or 'Flags:' after any annexes but before the list of departments consulted.
